messages:
Elena: Quick update — we rolled back the strict fncall validator in the EU canary ~10m ago after a spike in rejected tool responses from a small set of customers. Opening a thread for context and next steps.
Sam: saw that, thanks. Any correlation to a specific model variant or adapter?
Elena: early signal points to our new adapter that coerces arrays -> objects in a few legacy tool integrations. Rejection rate jumped from 0.4% -> 8% on canary hosts.
Kai: DeployBot: canary rollout 0.46 -> reverted to 0.45 by Elena (reason: fncall reject surge).
Priya: Oof. Do we have user-visible telemetry for "reject reason" on the Console? Product reports only see generic 4xx.
Sam: right now console shows "fncall_rejects" but not the validator reason. We capture reason in logs but not surfaced to customers due to PII risk.
Elena: the core ask — we need a way to show aggregated reject classes (e.g., missing-field, type-mismatch, unexpected-array) without exposing payloads. That would help support + devs triage before rolling back.
Kai: agree. For rollout policy, I'd rather have a soft mode that surfaces counts and top reasons to the account owner via the Console under a redacted "Validator Insights" panel. No raw JSON.
Sam: implementation question — do we tag telemetry on ingest with a small enum (reason_code) and route it to metrics + audit pipeline? That keeps heavy logs separate.
Elena: yes, reason_code enum is ideal. Also need sampling rules so we don't store many full payloads. Suggest: 100% reason_code, 1% raw payload snapshot, & only with customer opt-in for full traces.
Priya: billing implications — we bill for tool calls. When a fncall is rejected, do we charge the customer? Current ledger counts an attempt as billable. If we show rejects more prominently customers will escalate.
Sam: current policy: attempt billed. But we could add a "billable_status" tag in telemetry (billed:true/false) to help reconcile. Any change to billing would need legal & finance sign-off — but adding tags is low-risk.
Kai: UX for rollouts: add a Console toggle per customer to enable "strict validator" with an auto-rollback threshold (e.g., >2% rejects over 5m). That aligns product with canary behavior.
Elena: agreed. For short term: 1) Rollback stays. 2) Add reason_code enum into validation path and metrics within 48h. 3) Surface aggregated reasons in Console (no payloads). 4) Create runbook for support.
Priya: I'll draft runbook and open a finance thread about billing communication.
Sam: I'll sketch the telemetry schema. Proposal snippet: 
```
validator_event: {
  reason_code: "MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD | TYPE_MISMATCH | UNEXPECTED_ARRAY | UNKNOWN",
  validator_version: "v1.2.3",
  billed: "true|false",
  sample_id: "<opaque-id>"
}
```
Kai: impl note — keep reason_code string (not full path) to avoid leaking keys. sample_id must be k-anonymized.
Elena: assign action items: Sam -> telemetry PR, Kai -> console mock for aggregated view, Priya -> runbook + customer comm plan. I'll own rollout policy change.
Sam: tagging @DevOpsBot to spawn a metric alert for "fncall_reject_rate" if >2% for 5m in EU canary.
DevOpsBot: Alert created: fncall_reject_rate_eu_canary > 2% for 5m -> notify #eng-oncall and send email to eng-platform oncall.
Priya: thanks. Also, let's gate the Console feature behind a feature flag so we can A/B test messaging.
Elena: good call. One more: document the rollback rationale in the release notes so customers see why behavior changed.
Sam: noted. I'll add an entry to the release changelog.
Kai: any objections to re-rolling strict validator once reason_code telemetry is live and console surfacing is in place?
Priya: none from product, but legal wants a short blurb about PII redaction. I'll coordinate.
Elena: ok — we'll regroup in 48h with PRs and mocks. Closing thread for now, ping if anything urgent. :thumbsup:
